data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Dung semantics operate on abstract argumentation graphs, whereas DeepReason's schools operate on semantic conditioning of generative models."],"overturn_conditions":["DeepReason's semantic warrants cannot be formalized into strict attack relations.","Generative conditioning fundamentally tolerates ambiguity that invalidates Dung-style pruning."],"shared_structure":["Both systems rely on a unique skeptical extension to prune invalid elements.","Failure to enforce strict closure rules leads to unbounded accumulation of unpruned elements."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["Enforcing strict closure in DeepReason's criticism mechanism will replicate the guaranteed polynomial-time pruning seen in Dung grounded extensions."]},"claim":"Batch criticism fails to retire rival positions because it permits warrants that lack criterion-level forced choice, causing coverage debt to grow monotonically with rivalry size.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If warrants are restricted to criterion-level forced choice, attacks become decisive and rival positions retire.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the Dung grounded extension enforces strict closure rules, criticism automatically cascades and retires rivals.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Without criterion-level forced choice in warrants, critics can assert vague disanalogies or broad coverage claims that never trigger a decisive Dung grounded extension attack. Consequently, the number of accepted rival positions grows unbounded while attacks fail to form a unique skeptical extension, leaving coverage debt unpaid.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
